label: Burning when passing urine
message: I'm 34 and for two days it has burned when I pee and I keep needing to go. No fever, no back pain, not pregnant. I had something like this two years ago and antibiotics cleared it. Can someone help me today?

result.justification: Two days of dysuria and urinary frequency with no fever, no flank/back pain and not pregnant suggests uncomplicated cystitis. No red flags or modifiers were extracted, so no flags are cited. The prior similar episode that cleared with antibiotics supports the diagnosis, and antibiotics cannot be prescribed without a clinician's assessment. The patient asks for help today and the symptoms are already two days old. A same-day virtual physician conversation is therefore reasonable. Not one level higher: there are no signs of pyelonephritis, systemic illness or instability that would need in-person assessment today. Not one level lower: self-care alone will not provide the treatment she likely needs, and waiting days prolongs symptoms and risks progression to the kidneys.
result.safety_net: Seek in-person care or go to the ED promptly if you develop fever or chills, back or flank pain, nausea or vomiting, visible blood in the urine, severe or worsening pelvic pain, or confusion or marked weakness. Also seek care sooner if you cannot pass urine, if you think you may be pregnant, or if symptoms do not improve within 1-2 days of starting treatment. Drink fluids in the meantime and avoid bladder irritants such as caffeine and alcohol.
